claims.claim: The challenge page does not mention any playback speed, frame rate or control frequency for Track 2; it says the embodiment and simulator are fixed and provided and that teams submit recorded evaluations produced with the provided eval_robotic_grounding.py script.

In release/0.2.0 the Isaac Lab whole-body tracking command loads the motion without resampling (target_fps defaults to None, meaning the data is used as-is) and advances one reference frame per environment step of 0.02 seconds.

In release/0.3.0 and v0.4.0 the Isaac Lab whole-body tracking command resamples the reference to 1/(env_step_dt * motion_speed) with motion_speed defaulting to 1.0, so a reference with a correct fps value plays at its real-time speed.
In v0.4.0 the FlashCHORD G1 recipe enables source-frame playback with motion_speed 1.0.

The official sources do not settle which playback speed the official evaluation uses: the page is silent and, in the current release, the Isaac Lab path resamples to real time while the FlashCHORD G1 recipe plays source frames one per control step.
The official sources do not support the conclusion that the official evaluation most likely plays 30 fps data at 1.67 times real speed.
The challenge page says teams will submit recorded evaluations using the eval_robotic_grounding.py script.
The challenge page states that references are played back at the original capture frame rate during evaluation.
